title: Extensibly Causally Separable Processes Admit Realizations as Quantum Circuits with Classical Control of Causal Order
abstract: Indefinite causal order extends the conventional circuit paradigm by allowing local quantum operations to be connected without a predetermined global order. Within the process-matrix framework, it is characterized by causal nonseparability, whereas extensible causal separability (ECS) requires that, under arbitrary input-ancilla extensions, a process admit a recursive decomposition into components, each compatible with a particular operation acting first. Quantum circuits with classical control of causal order (QC-CC), in which previous outcomes dynamically determine which operation acts next, are known to generate ECS processes, but whether every ECS process admits such a realization has remained a longstanding open problem. We settle it through a generalized teleportation construction that realizes every multipartite ECS process as a QC-CC. We further establish consistency between ECS definitions for trivial and nontrivial global past and future systems. These results provide ECS with an exact operational interpretation and identify QC-CC as the complete circuit structure underlying this class of processes.
summary: This theoretical paper establishes a fundamental equivalence between two formalisms for quantum causality: Extensible Causal Separability (ECS) and Quantum Circuits with Classical Control of Causal Order (QC-CC). By proving that every ECS process can be realized as a QC-CC, the authors provide a complete operational understanding of this class of quantum processes. This result is crucial for understanding the limits of causal structure in quantum computation.
main_problem: The paper addresses the long-standing open problem of determining whether every Extensibly Causally Separable (ECS) quantum process admits a realization as a Quantum Circuit with Classical Control of Causal Order (QC-CC).
main_result: The authors prove the equivalence between ECS processes and QC-CC processes, establishing that QC-CC structures fully characterize the class of ECS processes.
method: The equivalence is established using a generalized teleportation construction and induction on the number of parties, relating abstract process-matrix definitions to concrete circuit structures.
model_or_system: The study concerns quantum processes described in the process-matrix framework, involving multiple local laboratories, global past, and global future systems. The core mathematical objects are the process matrices $W$ and their decomposition properties.
key_observables: The process matrix $W$, and its decomposition into components compatible with specific causal orderings.
important_parameters: The number of local laboratories ($N$), and the dimensionality of the input/output spaces ($P, F, A_k$).
main_assumptions: The analysis often considers deterministic processes, though extensions to probabilistic cases are also covered, relying on the existence of specific isometric encodings.
paper_structure: The paper builds by defining the abstract ECS concept, then defining the operational QC-CC model, and finally proving the equivalence through explicit constructions and inductive steps, covering both deterministic and probabilistic generalizations.
why_interesting: It provides a rigorous operational interpretation for abstract concepts of causality in quantum information, linking theoretical separability criteria (ECS) directly to realizable computational models (QC-CC).
